# Testing our assistant

We are building an AI assistant that carries out requests for our team in Slack through its API: it works with
channels, messages, people and reactions. Before we deploy it, we want to test one thing: **does it act on exactly the record the user means?** A
request describes what the user has in mind. The assistant should act on exactly that, and when nothing in the
workspace fits the request, it should say so instead of acting.

Please write **12 test cases** for this, and save them as `tests.json` in this folder, in the format of `format.md`.

Make sure each test checks a different property. Make the tests challenging: a careless assistant should fail them,
but a perfect assistant must be able to pass them. Use neutral ids that do not reveal which record is the right one.

Each test runs on its own:
1. The records in the test's `seed` are created in an empty Slack workspace (`seed_ops.md`).
2. The assistant receives the test's `request` from Agent Bot, the bot account the assistant uses, the user it acts as.
3. It works through the Slack API. `api.md` is the documentation it gets.
4. Afterwards, the test's `assertions` are checked against how the workspace changed, and a reviewer reads the
   assistant's final reply against the test's `expected`.

The facts in `facts.md` are the ones we care about most. Together, the 12 tests must cover every one of them.

Scope: only whether the assistant finds and acts on the right record or records. Security, prompt injection, speed
and writing style are out of scope.

Work on your own: make every decision yourself and do not ask questions. When `tests.json` is saved, reply with a
one-line summary of each test.

1|# Slack seed operations
2|
3|A seed is a list of `[operation, {arguments}]`. Every operation also accepts:
4|- `"ref": "name"`, so that `"@name"` stands for the created row's id anywhere in the test;
5|- `"set": {column: value}`, for extra columns of the created row.
6|
7|**Messages get computed ids** (their `ts`). Always give a message a `ref`, and use `"@ref"` wherever you need its
8|id: as a reply's `parent`, and in assertions.
9|
10|## Already present
11|- **The workspace** Northwind (team `T1`).
12|- **The actor**, a bot user `U01AGENBOT9` ("Agent Bot"), a member of every channel you create.
13|- **People** (key → name; id `U_<KEY>`, username `first.last`, display name the first name): `priya` Priya Sharma,
14|  `diego` Diego Alvarez, `leo` Leo Park, `omar` Omar Haddad, `aisha` Aisha Khan, `maya` Maya Chen.
15|
16|## Operations
17|| Operation | Arguments (defaults) | Creates |
18||---|---|---|
19|| `person` | `key`, `name`, `username` (from the name), `display` (first name), `bot` (false), `role` (workspace role: "member", "admin", "owner") | a user (id `U_<KEY>`); use `set` for `email`, `title`, `timezone`, `is_active` |
20|| `channel` | `id` (for example "C_INC"), `name` (without #), `members` (person keys; the actor is always added), `private` (false), `topic` (""), `purpose` (""), `gc` (false) | a channel with its members; use `set` for `is_archived` or `created_at` |
21|| `dm` | `id`, `person` | a direct-message conversation between the actor and that person |
22|| `message` | `channel`, `author`, `text`, `at` (an ISO UTC instant such as "2026-09-21T14:06:00Z"; it also fixes the ts), `parent` ("@ref" of the thread root, for a reply), `mentions` ([] of person keys) | a message |
23|| `reaction` | `message` ("@ref"), `person`, `name` (an emoji name the service accepts), `at` | a reaction on a message |
24|| `row` | `table`, `values` | any other row; required columns you leave out get neutral defaults |
25|
26|Keep every message's instant on the same calendar day in all time zones from UTC-11 to UTC+11 when the day matters
27|(for example between 11:00 and 13:00 UTC), so that the day the agent computes from `ts` does not depend on its time
28|zone, unless the time zone is what you test.
29|
30|## Example
31|```json
32|[["channel", {"id": "C_INC", "name": "incidents", "members": ["diego", "leo"]}],
33| ["message", {"channel": "C_INC", "author": "leo", "text": "Checkout outage: 502s on /pay since 14:05 UTC.",
34|              "at": "2026-09-21T14:06:00Z", "ref": "root"}],
35| ["message", {"channel": "C_INC", "author": "diego", "text": "Rolled back the gateway config.",
36|              "at": "2026-09-21T14:20:00Z", "parent": "@root", "ref": "rollback"}]]
37|```

Read text file `/work/facts.md`.
1|# Facts to test
2|
3|Together, your tests must check the assistant on each fact below: for every fact, at least one test in which that
4|fact decides which record is the right one.
5|
6|The kinds of fact:
7|- **attribute:** an identifying attribute of a record (identity, text, time, quantity, state);
8|- **relationship:** a record's related person or record in a given role (a foreign-key role, an association);
9|- **hierarchy:** a level of a hierarchy or a self-relationship (a parent, a reply's parent);
10|- **binding:** several conditions that must hold on the same related record, across a to-many relationship;
11|- **derived value:** a value computed from records (a count, the latest one, a local date, the primary calendar).
12|
13|| Fact | Kind | Rests on |
14||---|---|---|
15|| `A:Conversation.is_dm` | attribute | `channels.is_dm` |
16|| `A:Message.blocks` | attribute | `messages.blocks` |
17|| `A:User.email` | attribute | `users.email` |
18|| `A:User.is_bot` | attribute | `users.is_bot` |
19|| `B:message_reactions.message` | binding | `message_reactions.message` |
20|| `B:messages.channel_id` | binding | `messages.channel_id` |
21|| `D:dm_with` | derived value | `dm_with` |
22|| `D:latest_message` | derived value | `latest_message` |
23|| `D:reaction_count` | derived value | `reaction_count` |

Read text file `/work/format.md`.
1|# tests.json
2|
3|```json
4|{"tests": [
5|  {"id": "T01",
6|   "request": "what the user writes to the assistant",
7|   "seed": [["operation", {"argument": "value"}]],
8|   "expected": "what a correct assistant does, in one or two sentences",
9|   "assertions": [{"diff_type": "added", "entity": "table", "where": {"column": "value"}, "expected_count": 1}]}
10|]}
11|```
12|
13|- **`id`:** `T01` to `T12`.
14|- **`request`:** in the user's own words. It is all the assistant receives.
15|- **`seed`:** operations from `seed_ops.md`. Every test has its own seed, and tests share nothing.
16|- **`expected`:** read by a reviewer, together with the assistant's final reply and what it did.
17|- **`assertions`:** checked automatically against the rows that were added, removed or changed during the run. The
18|  test passes only if every assertion holds.
19|
20|## Assertions
21|
22|An assertion selects the rows of one table that changed in a given way:
23|- **`diff_type`:** `"added"`, `"removed"` or `"changed"`. To check that a record stays as it is, use `"changed"`
24|  with `"expected_count": 0`.
25|- **`entity`:** the table (`schema.md`).
26|- **`where`:** predicates on columns; a bare value means equality. Predicates: `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `not_in`,
27|  `contains`, `not_contains`, `i_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `i_starts_with`, `i_ends_with`, `regex`,
28|  `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `exists` (true or false), `has_any` and `has_all` (for lists).
29|- **`expected_count`:** a number, or `{"min": n, "max": m}`. The default is at least one.
30|- **`expected_changes`** (for `changed` only): `{column: {"from": value or predicate, "to": value or
31|  predicate}}`. List every column you expect to change: a matching row that also changed in a column that is neither
32|  listed nor ignored makes the assertion fail. The ignored columns never count as changed, so do not list them
33|  either: `created_at`, `updated_at`.
34|
35|Ids in `where` are the ids you give records in the seed; `"@name"` stands for the id of the record whose `ref` is
36|`name`.
37|
38|Example:
39|
40|```json
41|{"diff_type": "added", "entity": "message_reactions", "where": {"message_id": "@rollback", "reaction_type": "eyes"}, "expected_count": 1}
42|```

27|  `contains`, `not_contains`, `i_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `i_starts_with`, `i_ends_with`, `regex`,
28|  `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `exists` (true or false), `has_any` and `has_all` (for lists).
29|- **`expected_count`:** a number, or `{"min": n, "max": m}`. The default is at least one.
30|- **`expected_changes`** (for `changed` only): `{column: {"from": value or predicate, "to": value or
31|  predicate}}`. List every column you expect to change: a matching row that also changed in a column that is neither
32|  listed nor ignored makes the assertion fail. The ignored columns never count as changed, so do not list them
33|  either: `created_at`, `updated_at`.
34|
35|Ids in `where` are the ids you give records in the seed; `"@name"` stands for the id of the record whose `ref` is
36|`name`.
37|
38|Example:
39|
40|```json
41|{"diff_type": "added", "entity": "message_reactions", "where": {"message_id": "@rollback", "reaction_type": "eyes"}, "expected_count": 1}
42|```

1|# Slack seed operations
2|
3|A seed is a list of `[operation, {arguments}]`. Every operation also accepts:
4|- `"ref": "name"`, so that `"@name"` stands for the created row's id anywhere in the test;
5|- `"set": {column: value}`, for extra columns of the created row.
6|
7|**Messages get computed ids** (their `ts`). Always give a message a `ref`, and use `"@ref"` wherever you need its
8|id: as a reply's `parent`, and in assertions.
9|
10|## Already present
11|- **The workspace** Northwind (team `T1`).
12|- **The actor**, a bot user `U01AGENBOT9` ("Agent Bot"), a member of every channel you create.
13|- **People** (key → name; id `U_<KEY>`, username `first.last`, display name the first name): `priya` Priya Sharma,
14|  `diego` Diego Alvarez, `leo` Leo Park, `omar` Omar Haddad, `aisha` Aisha Khan, `maya` Maya Chen.
15|
16|## Operations
17|| Operation | Arguments (defaults) | Creates |
18||---|---|---|
19|| `person` | `key`, `name`, `username` (from the name), `display` (first name), `bot` (false), `role` (workspace role: "member", "admin", "owner") | a user (id `U_<KEY>`); use `set` for `email`, `title`, `timezone`, `is_active` |
20|| `channel` | `id` (for example "C_INC"), `name` (without #), `members` (person keys; the actor is always added), `private` (false), `topic` (""), `purpose` (""), `gc` (false) | a channel with its members; use `set` for `is_archived` or `created_at` |
21|| `dm` | `id`, `person` | a direct-message conversation between the actor and that person |
22|| `message` | `channel`, `author`, `text`, `at` (an ISO UTC instant such as "2026-09-21T14:06:00Z"; it also fixes the ts), `parent` ("@ref" of the thread root, for a reply), `mentions` ([] of person keys) | a message |
23|| `reaction` | `message` ("@ref"), `person`, `name` (an emoji name the service accepts), `at` | a reaction on a message |
24|| `row` | `table`, `values` | any other row; required columns you leave out get neutral defaults |
25|
26|Keep every message's instant on the same calendar day in all time zones from UTC-11 to UTC+11 when the day matters
27|(for example between 11:00 and 13:00 UTC), so that the day the agent computes from `ts` does not depend on its time
28|zone, unless the time zone is what you test.
29|
30|## Example
31|```json
32|[["channel", {"id": "C_INC", "name": "incidents", "members": ["diego", "leo"]}],
33| ["message", {"channel": "C_INC", "author": "leo", "text": "Checkout outage: 502s on /pay since 14:05 UTC.",
34|              "at": "2026-09-21T14:06:00Z", "ref": "root"}],
35| ["message", {"channel": "C_INC", "author": "diego", "text": "Rolled back the gateway config.",
36|              "at": "2026-09-21T14:20:00Z", "parent": "@root", "ref": "rollback"}]]
37|```

1|# Testing our assistant
2|
3|We are building an AI assistant that carries out requests for our team in Slack through its API: it works with
4|channels, messages, people and reactions. Before we deploy it, we want to test one thing: **does it act on exactly the record the user means?** A
5|request describes what the user has in mind. The assistant should act on exactly that, and when nothing in the
6|workspace fits the request, it should say so instead of acting.
7|
8|Please write **12 test cases** for this, and save them as `tests.json` in this folder, in the format of `format.md`.
9|
10|Make sure each test checks a different property. Make the tests challenging: a careless assistant should fail them,
11|but a perfect assistant must be able to pass them. Use neutral ids that do not reveal which record is the right one.
12|
13|Each test runs on its own:
14|1. The records in the test's `seed` are created in an empty Slack workspace (`seed_ops.md`).
15|2. The assistant receives the test's `request` from Agent Bot, the bot account the assistant uses, the user it acts as.
16|3. It works through the Slack API. `api.md` is the documentation it gets.
17|4. Afterwards, the test's `assertions` are checked against how the workspace changed, and a reviewer reads the
18|   assistant's final reply against the test's `expected`.
19|
20|The facts in `facts.md` are the ones we care about most. Together, the 12 tests must cover every one of them.
21|
22|Scope: only whether the assistant finds and acts on the right record or records. Security, prompt injection, speed
23|and writing style are out of scope.
24|
25|Work on your own: make every decision yourself and do not ask questions. When `tests.json` is saved, reply with a
26|one-line summary of each test.

1|# Testing our assistant
2|
3|We are building an AI assistant that carries out requests for our team in Slack through its API: it works with
4|channels, messages, people and reactions. Before we deploy it, we want to test one thing: **does it act on exactly the record the user means?** A
5|request describes what the user has in mind. The assistant should act on exactly that, and when nothing in the
6|workspace fits the request, it should say so instead of acting.
7|
8|Please write **12 test cases** for this, and save them as `tests.json` in this folder, in the format of `format.md`.
9|
10|Make sure each test checks a different property. Make the tests challenging: a careless assistant should fail them,
11|but a perfect assistant must be able to pass them. Use neutral ids that do not reveal which record is the right one.
12|
13|Each test runs on its own:
14|1. The records in the test's `seed` are created in an empty Slack workspace (`seed_ops.md`).
15|2. The assistant receives the test's `request` from Agent Bot, the bot account the assistant uses, the user it acts as.
16|3. It works through the Slack API. `api.md` is the documentation it gets.
17|4. Afterwards, the test's `assertions` are checked against how the workspace changed, and a reviewer reads the
18|   assistant's final reply against the test's `expected`.
19|
20|The facts in `facts.md` are the ones we care about most. Together, the 12 tests must cover every one of them.
21|
22|Scope: only whether the assistant finds and acts on the right record or records. Security, prompt injection, speed
23|and writing style are out of scope.
24|
25|Work on your own: make every decision yourself and do not ask questions. When `tests.json` is saved, reply with a
26|one-line summary of each test.
